title: The people
frame: This is written to the people you walked with. Say it to them.

slots.stem: To the people I walked with, I am
slots.prompt: It is done. Start with them. One word for what you feel toward them now — the row has some — then why, in a few words.
slots.ex: To the people I walked with, I am tired and grateful. You heard the worst of it and you kept showing up.

slots.stem: What I saw in you was
slots.prompt: Name the gold. Not what they did for you — who they showed themselves to be. One thing, said plainly.
slots.ex: What I saw in you was people who told the truth before it was safe to.

title: Where I started
frame: Start where it began. Three lines, and a picture anyone could see.

slots.stem: When I started, I was
slots.prompt: Go back to the day it began — the first meeting, the first session, the first week. Where were you: the place, the time of day, what was going on around you? A picture, not a label.
slots.ex: When I started, I was sitting in the truck in the driveway, not ready to go in the house.

slots.stem: What I told myself was
slots.prompt: Now the sentence you were living on back then — the one you said to yourself to get through the day. “I’ve got it handled.” “Nobody needs to know.” Short.
slots.ex: What I told myself was that I had it handled.

slots.stem: What nobody knew was
slots.prompt: And the part of it no one could see from outside.
slots.ex: What nobody knew was how long it had been going on.

title: What changed
frame: Time didn’t change you. The work you did with them did. Say what is different, in three places: body, soul, spirit.

slots.stem: What came in through my eyes and ears was
slots.prompt: Everything that reached you through your eyes and ears — any sound or sight you control. What was coming in?
slots.ex: What came in through my eyes and ears was a screen at midnight and voices telling me I was the only one.

slots.stem: What I take in now is
slots.prompt: The same eyes and ears. Now you are the gatekeeper for what comes in. What do you let in — a first thing in the morning, a habit that has held, a practice you took up? Pick from the row, or write your own.
slots.ex: What I take in now is a walk before the house wakes up and a chapter of John read out loud.
slots.rowNote: From Richard Foster’s Celebration of Discipline.

slots.stem: What is being renewed in me is
slots.prompt: Pick where it is happening, then say what is new there.
slots.ex: What is being renewed in me is how I see my father — the word used to mean absence.
words: how I name what I feel
what I do first in the morning

slots.stem: Between me and God, what is growing is
slots.prompt: Spirit is where you and God meet. Of faith, hope and love, which one grew — and what does it look like in an ordinary week?
slots.ex: Between me and God, what is growing is hope. I expect Him to show up now.

title: Then and now
frame: Two of your lines. What happened between them?

slots.prompt: A day, a place, something said or done. One or two sentences; the row has some ways to start.
slots.ex: What happened next was a week I almost skipped, and didn’t.

bridge.b: What I take in now is

title: What God did
scene: I will turn their mourning into joy; I will comfort them, and give them gladness for sorrow. — Jeremiah 31:13
frame: If it is still quiet and the struggle is still here, say that. It is not failure. This takes years, not weeks, and God’s answer may be as small as a room with people in it.

slots.stem: You saw me
slots.prompt: Not the story itself — the day you told it. What did they do with it? In a group like that, shame has no place to hide.
slots.ex: You saw me the day I said the thing I had never said out loud, and nobody looked away.

slots.stem: What I expected was
slots.prompt: Before you said it out loud — what did you brace for? Being judged, being handled, the group going quiet.
slots.ex: What I expected was the group to go cold.

slots.stem: What happened instead was
slots.prompt: What they did. Say it plainly; it is the part someone else needs to hear.
slots.ex: What happened instead was someone said “me too.”

slots.stem: I asked Him for
slots.prompt: What did you ask God for at the start? Say it the way you said it then. Not every ask is answered yet.
slots.ex: I asked Him for it to stop.

slots.stem: What God did was
slots.prompt: Say what He did, not what you did. For some it is this: a room with people in it, and what got named there. If nothing has moved yet, say that — it is true, and it belongs here.
slots.ex: What God did was put me in a room with people willing to walk with me.

title: Seen and answered
frame: Two more pairs of your lines. What happened between each?

slots.prompt: The thing nobody knew, and the day they saw you. What happened in between — a day, a place, something said or done?
slots.ex: It took weeks, but one night I said it out loud before I could talk myself out of it.

slots.prompt: What you asked Him for, and what He did. How long did it take, and what did the waiting look like?
slots.ex: While that was going on, I kept asking, and for a month nothing changed except that I kept showing up.

title: What I take with me
scene: Jesus turned and saw them following and said to them, “What are you seeking?” — John 1:38
frame: Jesus’ first words in John’s Gospel are a question, asked of two who followed Him. Answer it for a year from now.

slots.stem: My hope for the future is
slots.prompt: A year down the trail — what do you want to be true? Say it as someone who means to get there.
slots.ex: My hope for the future is to be someone my kids can tell the truth to.

slots.stem: What I will miss is
slots.prompt: An ending is a loss, even a good one. Say what aches. It is holy ground, not weakness.
slots.ex: What I will miss is knowing that once a week someone would ask.

slots.stem: What I ask of you is
slots.prompt: It is done. What do you need from them now?
slots.ex: What I ask of you is to keep asking me the question, even when I say I’m fine.

slots.stem: Going forward, with this group, I will
slots.prompt: Yes or no — say it plainly and own it. Both are honorable. A goodbye said well is an ending done right.
slots.ex: Going forward, with this group, I will say goodbye. Thank you. I am taking this with me.

title: How I’ll keep it
frame: Not the whole life. One small step, a way to see that it held, and what you will do when you drift.

slots.stem: The one small thing I will try this month is
slots.prompt: Not the whole life. One small thing, repeated, that moves you one degree — something you could start tomorrow.
slots.ex: The one small thing I will try this month is one chapter of John before my phone.

slots.stem: I’ll know it has held when
slots.prompt: How will you know? Something you could see or count, four weeks from now.
slots.ex: I’ll know it has held when I have read a chapter before my phone four mornings a week, four weeks in a row.

slots.stem: I’ll know I’ve drifted when
slots.prompt: Name the sign before it comes — what you will be doing, and what you will be feeling. Pick from the rows, or write your own.
slots.ex: I’ll know I’ve drifted when my phone goes quiet and I tell myself I’m fine.

slots.stem: The voice that calls me back says
slots.prompt: Not a name — the words. What does it say?
slots.ex: The voice that calls me back says, “They heard the worst and stayed.”

slots.stem: I will answer it by
slots.prompt: The days are not the achievement. Whatever you did that made the days is the achievement. Find it, name it out loud, and do it again. Pick one, or write your own.
slots.ex: I will answer it by a text to one of them, that day.
